sampling_model.design: Independent and identically distributed observational or fixed-randomization sampling from \(P\); the known benchmark \(b_a\) is conceptually distinct from the observational propensity \(e_a\).
sampling_model.treatment: A fixed finite action set \(\mathcal A=\{0,\ldots,J-1\}\) under consistency, conditional exchangeability, and uniform overlap.
sampling_model.overlap: \(e_a(X)\ge\epsilon\) and \(b_a(X)\ge\epsilon_b\) almost surely for every action, with \(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}b_a(X)=1\) almost surely.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: A fixed number of balanced folds; outcome and propensity learners are trained outside each evaluation fold, attain \(L^2(P_X)\) rates \(r_{m,n}\) and \(r_{e,n}\), and satisfy \(\sqrt n r_{m,n}r_{e,n}\to0\).

body.tldr: On the common regular finite-action benchmark-centered softmax submodel of FangRidderXie2026, this proposal's direct KL penalty coordinate \(c\) maps to their optimization penalty \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\), while their reported normalized preference is \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\). The field-level contribution is a quantitative empirical replacement template separating nuisance-product bias, nuisance-sum \(L^2(P)\) error, and same-sample path plug-in error; a checkable envelope and softmax-path entropy condition; the resulting joint uniform optimizer--welfare--divergence influence process and stacked shared-multiplier law; a simultaneous tube valid after any measurable penalty choice; and uniform Hessian-quadratic regret calibration. A measurable ridge fallback makes every finite-sample estimated influence, covariance, and multiplier object total and is uniformly inactive with probability tending to one. Path-uniform interiority, three-derivative smoothness, and curvature are stronger conditions maintained by this note, not conditions attributed to the fixed-penalty comparator. Benchmark weights form a positive probability kernel, so \(K\) is KL divergence and \(\pi_0=b\). Inverse-set reporting is a direct application corollary of RenTelschowSchwartzman2024, and the deterministic-penalty result is only a non-novel sanity reduction to FangRidderXie2026 Theorems 2 and 5.

project_justification.gap: FangRidderXie2026 Theorem 1 gives the efficient influence function and bound, Theorem 2 gives the fixed-penalty quadratic-regret law, Theorem 4 treats estimated-propensity IPW, and Theorem 5 gives the efficient doubly robust optimizer and quadratic-regret limit, all at fixed optimization penalty \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}>0\). With \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\), hence \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\), and with its admissible rules restricted to the common finite-action benchmark-centered softmax subclass \(\{\pi_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\), it does not supply joint inference over the direct penalty path \(c\in\mathcal C\). Generic orthogonal-band theory assumes rather than verifies the uniform estimated-influence replacement needed for fold-specific learned influences evaluated along the same-sample implicit optimizer path.
project_justification.niche: The missing object on this common softmax submodel is a checkable path-entropy and replacement argument leading to one stacked shared-multiplier law that respects covariance across preferences, separates oracle-frontier uncertainty from fitted-rule evaluation, and protects selection from the displayed curve.
project_justification.fill: The project states the stronger path-uniform interiority, three-derivative smoothness, and curvature conditions explicitly; derives their finite-action softmax sufficient-condition routes; proves product-bias, sum-radius, path plug-in, envelope, and entropy bounds for the empirical replacement condition; uses a measurable ridge fallback that equals ordinary Hessian inversion uniformly with probability tending to one; obtains the joint uniform influence and shared-multiplier laws; forms a conservative simultaneous tube; and calibrates uniform second-order regret. The inverse correspondence is obtained afterward by direct application of RenTelschowSchwartzman2024.

body.related_work: FangRidderXie2026 supplies the admissible-rule framework and three-arm commitment-savings frontier. Its Theorem 1 gives the efficient influence function and bound, Theorem 2 the fixed-penalty quadratic-regret law, Theorem 4 the estimated-propensity IPW result, and Theorem 5 the efficient doubly robust optimizer and quadratic-regret limit. The common model here restricts that framework to its regular finite-action benchmark-centered softmax subclass \(\{\pi_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\): this proposal's direct penalty coordinate maps as \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\), and the comparator's reported preference is \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\). The new claim is uniformity over this direct penalty path, not a broader treatment class or a superset of their admissible rules. Their fixed-penalty interiority, two-derivative smoothness, and pointwise Hessian condition do not establish this note's uniform interiority, uniform three-derivative condition, or uniform curvature floor; those stronger hypotheses are explicitly introduced here, with compact-path and bounded-softmax sufficient-condition arguments. BelloniChernozhukovChetverikovWei2018 supplies the generic uniform Bahadur and estimated-score multiplier architecture; the present result is informed by that theorem and contributes explicit nuisance-product conditional-bias, nuisance-sum \(L^2(P)\)-radius, path plug-in, envelope, and softmax-path entropy bounds for fold-specific estimated influences along an implicit same-sample optimizer path. A single measurable ridge convention totalizes the estimated influence, covariance, shared-multiplier, and quadratic-regret objects and is shown to equal ordinary inversion uniformly on an event whose probability tends to one. ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML supplies orthogonality, foldwise conditioning, and nuisance product-rate logic for regular causal targets. ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2016 supplies Gaussian and multiplier coupling after deterministic entropy control. ChenFang2019 supplies the second-order delta method and the warning that standard bootstraps fail under first-order degeneracy; the proposed quadratic multiplier process is informed by that result. FirpoGalvaoParker2023 studies uniform inference after marginal optimization in nonregular value-function problems, whereas the explicitly maintained uniqueness and path-uniform curvature make the present implicit optimizer regular. PolicyLearningWithConfidence2026 already establishes a broad reporting-guarantee principle for selected policies, so this proposal claims only the KL-frontier-specific joint process and eventwise measurable-selection consequence. RenTelschowSchwartzman2024 supplies the inverse-set theorem, of which the frontier inversion is a direct application corollary; YamazoeNaito2024 supplies a geometric curve-region comparison. Neither inversion nor the deterministic-penalty reduction is part of the novelty kernel.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The central unresolved proof obligation is to derive \(\delta_n\le C_{\mathrm{sm}}\{r_{m,n}+r_{e,n}+r_{m,n}r_{e,n}+\upsilon_n\}+o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) and \(\upsilon_n=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) for the fold-specific estimated influence stack evaluated along \(\widehat\theta_c\). The checkable envelope and softmax-path entropy lemma makes this shrinking radius sufficient for conditional multiplier replacement; it must not treat overlapping training complements as independent. The maintained path-uniform interiority, three-derivative smoothness, and curvature are stronger than the comparator's fixed-penalty regularity and remain explicit conditions. The measurable ridge fallback is a finite-sample totalization, not an assumption that empirical Hessians are invertible; its asymptotic irrelevance requires the stated uniform Hessian-consistency lemma and the good event \(\mathcal E_n\). The fixed positive direct-penalty interval excludes vanishing penalties, weak overlap, growing parameter dimension, adaptive sampling, and nonunique optimizers. The tube covers the oracle frontier and, when separately stacked, implemented-rule evaluation; these influences must not be interchanged. The quadratic claim concerns penalized regret, not unpenalized welfare loss.
body.honest_scope: The open content is the quantitative uniform empirical replacement bound for fold-specific estimated influences evaluated along the same-sample optimizer path, with nuisance-product bias, nuisance-sum \(L^2(P)\) error, and the explicitly defined path plug-in radius kept separate. The envelope and softmax-path entropy lemma makes that condition sufficient for the stacked shared-multiplier approximation. The implicit-function expansion and uniform quadratic mapping then deliver the joint frontier law, simultaneous post-selection tube, and uniform regret calibration under the note's explicitly stronger path-uniform interiority, three-derivative smoothness, and curvature conditions. A measurable ridge convention makes every plug-in object total, while uniform Hessian consistency and \(P(\mathcal E_n)\to1\) make it equal ordinary inversion simultaneously over the path asymptotically. RenTelschowSchwartzman2024 directly supplies the inverse-set corollary, while deterministic evaluation at one direct penalty is only a non-novel sanity reduction to FangRidderXie2026 Theorems 2 and 5 after setting \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\), hence \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\), and restricting its admissible rules to \(\{\pi_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\). Genuine tangencies or self-intersections do not occur on a nonconstant frontier under the maintained identified softmax geometry. No broader treatment class, result for \(c\to0\), or Banach-space efficiency optimality for tube width is asserted.
